View (looking westward) of buildings at Laguna pueblo, located on on the Rio Laguna river (a tributary of the Rio Grande), about sixty miles west of Isleta.  According to James Stevenson's original note for this photograph (prepared circa 1885), Laguna's 'earlier location was thirty miles north of the present village, but from time to time during the last three or four centuries changes have been made until the present location of the village was reached. [...] The photograph shows quite clearly the beauty and compactness of this typical pueblo.
Portrait of a man (named Jose Paisano) from Laguna pueblo, sitting, wearing European clothing.

Plough with iron share. The plough is carved from wood. The share is nailed to the pointed foot of the plough, the foot is square in section with a projection on the top. The top of the foot is perforated in three places. A wooden peg and the plough handle are socketed into two of the perforations. [AB [OPS Move] 31/1/2017]
